text:
jordan: Quick ping  I ran the next-edge-llama starter against the eval harness and it's flaky. Short repro: deploy example in local dev, run harness, sometimes the output is cut off.

priya: Symptoms? 401 or stream close?

jordan: Starts with a 401 during token rotation window then our SDK retries but the retry goes out with the old token. Result is a partial stream and harness flags it truncated.

matt_dev: Which SDK version is the example using?

jordan: package.json pins @redwood/sdk@0.12.0. We shipped a refresh-concurrency fix in 0.12.3.

priya: Two-pronged fix: bump the SDK in the example to 0.12.3, and add a guard in the API route to fail fast with a readable error when the key is missing in edge runtimes. Example guard: if (!process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY) throw new Error('REDWOOD_API_KEY missing: set .env.local or use node runtime').

matt_dev: Also add a tiny msw-based test in the example that simulates token expiry: first /v1/chat returns 401, token endpoint returns refreshed token, subsequent /v1/chat succeeds and full stream is returned. Fast and deterministic.

jordan: Good. On the harness side, treat 401 as potentially transient during rotation and retry with exponential backoff up to 3 times before failing. That mirrors real deployment behavior.

ci-bot: Created issue #4027: "next-edge-llama: token refresh race causing intermittent truncated eval output" assigned to matt_dev  https://issues.redwood/4027

devex-bot: PR created in examples/next-edge-llama: bump SDK -> 0.12.3; add env guard; add msw integration test.

priya: Once PR lands I'll re-run the harness and mark the CI job non-flaky. Thanks for the catch. :sparkles:
